title: Quantum motility-induced phase separation
summary: Motility-induced phase separation (MIPS) describes a central clustering phenomenon in active matter systems where particles spontaneously separate into dense and dilute phases even in the absence of interparticle attractive forces. Recent theoretical and experimental efforts have taken the first steps to extend active matter concepts to the quantum level. However, whether a genuine quantum analog of MIPS exists and how quantum coherence would compete or cooperate with the dissipative self-propulsion has remained open so far.
